answer: A voyage provision-market bond covers one voyage per identity. The applicant locks 60 credits, buys a provision bundle at the inlet market, and posts its receipt on the lotus board, publishing prices for recomputation. The inlet auditor checks each receipt: a wrong key, a mismatched price, or a reused bundle burns the bond. Prices rise with order depth: bundle k costs 35+3(k-1), so the 1000th pays 3032 and 1000 fakes pay 1,533,500 plus 60,000 locked bonds. A rented-provision ring fails on wrong-key receipts. An honest agent pays 35 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
